UULTIS /SPACE / 4 MIN READ

A room in proportion.

Start with the way you move, then find the piece that belongs.

Uultis digital experience · Editorial guide

IN THIS ARTICLEBegin with everyday life.Measure the room and the route.Compare a few different forms.Make the final check with the technical sheet.

Begin with everyday life.

Before choosing a silhouette, list what the space needs to do. A reading corner, a conversation area and a dining space each ask different things of a piece. Note the routes between doors and the furniture you already use.

Measure the room and the route.

Record the available floor area, door openings and the path into the room. Mark a proposed footprint with removable tape. Walk around it, pull out nearby chairs and check that doors and drawers can still open. A photograph alone cannot tell you how a piece will fit.

Compare a few different forms.

A round table introduces a different rhythm from a long rectangular surface. Compare Star and Sintonia in the Room Studio, then try a bench such as Trapézio. Orbit the study and use the isolated view to focus on the outline. Changing the light can help you read the shape, but does not predict the lighting in your actual room.

Make the final check with the technical sheet.

The studio is an exploratory tool. Some models use approximate study dimensions; their controls say so. Check the specific size, finish and product variant in its technical document, and confirm any remaining details with the team before ordering.
